newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says two groups dropped cellular phone bids.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says two groups dropped cellular phone bids.

text.p: Two consortia have dropped their bids for licenses to operate B Band cellular telephone concessions in Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais states, the Communications Ministry said on Thursday.

Ministry spokesman Francisco Mendonca told Reuters the GFTT group withdrew its bid for the Area 3 concession, covering Rio, while the Tess group pulled out of the running for the Area 4 concession in Minas Gerais.
"They've decided not to renew their offers as required under the tender details," Mendonca said.
The B Band bid specifications require bidders to renew their offers every 60 days until a winner is picked.
Presented in early April, B Band bids were opened in early June. The deadline for renewing proposals was 1800 local/1700 EDT/2100 GMT on Thursday, officials said.

Mendonca said he did not know what prompted GFTT and Tess to withdraw from the bidding. He said both groups had maintained their offers for other B Band licenses. "They still are bidding for other areas," he said.

GFTT -- comprised of France Telecom, the Brazilian telecom venture Teldin and the local bank Garantia -- has also bid on the Area 5 license, covering the southern states of Parana and Santa Catarina, and Area 10, covering six northeastern state.
Tess -- made up of Sweden's Telia and Brazil's Airline Celular and C.R. Alameida -- has made an offer for Area six, covering the southern state of Rio Grande do Sul.
Mendonca also said President Fernando Henrique Cardoso was expected to sign contracts Wednesday with the BCP SA group, which includes Bell South Corp, and the Vicunha Telecomunicacoes SA consortium.
BCP won a license to operate in Area 1 -- the largest -- covering Sao Paulo city, while Vicunha won the Area 9 license for the northeastern states of Bahia and Sergipe.
